summary: The study investigates the preparation and calcination effects on the reducibility, dispersion, and activity of Co/SiO2 catalysts prepared via atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and impregnation. The ALE process uses Co(acac)3 as a precursor, while impregnation uses Co(NO3)2. The calcination step significantly affects reducibility, with uncalcined ALE catalysts showing higher reducibility and activity in toluene hydrogenation compared to calcined ones.
evidence: The Co/SiO2 catalysts were prepared by a gas-phase deposition technique, atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), using Co(acac)3 as precursor and by impregnation from Co(NO3)2. The calcination step after the last Co(acac)3 reaction step was omitted for uncalcined catalysts, leading to higher reducibility and activity in toluene hydrogenation.
